blocks.section: Chapter Six. Puryaṣṭaka: the eightfold fortress of the delud

blocks.directed: The gross embodiment is no longer present.

blocks.text: But the limitations and dispositions constituting the finite subject have not necessarily been destroyed.
blocks.directed: But the limitations and dispositions constituting the finite subject have not necessarily been destroyed.

blocks.section: Chapter Six. Puryaṣṭaka: the eightfold fortress of the delud

blocks.directed: The subtle organization becomes relevant to the continuation of experience and the acquisition of another body.

blocks.section: Chapter Six. Puryaṣṭaka: the eightfold fortress of the delud

blocks.text: So when we ask what transmigrates, we must distinguish the conditioned individual continuity from universal consciousness.

blocks.directed: ### 6.3 Why a fortress?

blocks.text: And verse 19.7 introduces a restriction concerning unresolved impurity and karmic embodiment.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The practice is not presented as a universal service for every person who decides they fancy leaving the planet.
blocks.directed: The practice is not presented as a universal service for every person who decides they fancy leaving the planet.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Within the text's own system, spiritual qualification matters.
blocks.directed: Within the text's own system, spiritual qualification matters.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Why?
blocks.directed: Why?

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Because the relation between karma, impurity, initiation and liberation is not incidental.
blocks.directed: Because the relation between karma, impurity, initiation and liberation is not incidental.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: It defines the conditions under which a particular transformation is possible.
blocks.directed: It defines the conditions under which a particular transformation is possible.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The ritual is not presented as a mechanical bypass of the entire metaphysical architecture.
blocks.directed: The ritual is not presented as a mechanical bypass of the entire metaphysical architecture.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Abhinavagupta is not saying:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Abhinavagupta is not saying:

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: "Doesn't matter what state you're in. Just apply the sacred breathing apparatus and enjoy unlimited Śiva."
blocks.directed: [short pause] "Doesn't matter what state you're in. Just apply the sacred breathing apparatus and enjoy unlimited Śiva."

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: He is working within an extremely elaborate theory of grace and bondage.
blocks.directed: He is working within an extremely elaborate theory of grace and bondage.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: And the eligibility conditions are part of that theory.
blocks.directed: And the eligibility conditions are part of that theory.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: ### 7.2 What is the guru actually transforming?
blocks.directed: ### 7.2 What is the guru actually transforming?

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: In *Tantrasāra* 15.2, the guru ritually establishes and purifies the *adhvan*, the paths or dimensions through which manifestation is articulated.
blocks.directed: In *Tantrasāra* 15.2, the guru ritually establishes and purifies the *adhvan*, the paths or dimensions through which manifestation is articulated.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The traditional system distinguishes six such paths: three associated broadly with the expressive or linguistic order, and three with the objective order of manifestation.
blocks.directed: The traditional system distinguishes six such paths: three associated broadly with the expressive or linguistic order, and three with the objective order of manifestation.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The standard sixfold scheme consists of *varṇa* \(phonemes), *mantra*, *pada* \(words), *kalā* \(powers or divisions), *tattva* \(principles of reality) and *bhuvana* \(worlds).
blocks.directed: The standard sixfold scheme consists of *varṇa* \(phonemes), *mantra*, *pada* \(words), *kalā* \(powers or divisions), *tattva* \(principles of reality) and *bhuvana* \(worlds).

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: These aren't simply six levels of your spinal cord.
blocks.directed: These aren't simply six levels of your spinal cord.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: They're ways of organizing the totality of manifest reality.
blocks.directed: They're ways of organizing the totality of manifest reality.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Why does this matter?
blocks.directed: Why does this matter?

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Because initiation in this tradition is conceived as far more than blessing a particular bodily organ.
blocks.directed: Because initiation in this tradition is conceived as far more than blessing a particular bodily organ.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The disciple's finite existence is understood as embedded within the cosmic structures of manifestation.
blocks.directed: The disciple's finite existence is understood as embedded within the cosmic structures of manifestation.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The ritual purification is therefore directed toward the bonds connecting the individual to that structured world.
blocks.directed: The ritual purification is therefore directed toward the bonds connecting the individual to that structured world.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: It seeks to transform the individual's relation to the entire order of limitation.
blocks.directed: It seeks to transform the individual's relation to the entire order of limitation.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: That's considerably more ambitious than an energy massage.
blocks.directed: That's considerably more ambitious than an energy massage.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The guru is symbolically and ritually addressing the entire cosmos as it is articulated through the finite individual.
blocks.directed: The guru is symbolically and ritually addressing the entire cosmos as it is articulated through the finite individual.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: ### 7.3 Kālarātrī: death's extremely unwelcoming assistant
blocks.directed: ### 7.3 Kālarātrī: death's extremely unwelcoming assistant

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The goddess Kālarātrī appears as a fierce force that severs bonds.
blocks.directed: The goddess Kālarātrī appears as a fierce force that severs bonds.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: In *Tantrāloka* 19.10-14 and *Tantrasāra* 15.2, the ritual account associates her with the cutting of *marman* bonds.
blocks.directed: In *Tantrāloka* 19.10-14 and *Tantrasāra* 15.2, the ritual account associates her with the cutting of *marman* bonds.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: A *marman* is a vital junction or vulnerable point.
blocks.directed: A *marman* is a vital junction or vulnerable point.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The ritual imagery is fierce, involving the dissolution of connections that bind the individual to embodied existence.
blocks.directed: The ritual imagery is fierce, involving the dissolution of connections that bind the individual to embodied existence.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Within the historical system, the symbolism is linked to an actual deathbed ritual whose efficacy is asserted by its practitioners.
blocks.directed: Within the historical system, the symbolism is linked to an actual deathbed ritual whose efficacy is asserted by its practitioners.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: But its metaphysical meaning is more general.
blocks.directed: But its metaphysical meaning is more general.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The finite person is not merely a bundle of physical structures.
blocks.directed: The finite person is not merely a bundle of physical structures.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: They are bound within a network of cosmic and karmic relations.
blocks.directed: They are bound within a network of cosmic and karmic relations.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The rite represents those bonds as capable of being severed through the intervention of divine Śakti.
blocks.directed: The rite represents those bonds as capable of being severed through the intervention of divine Śakti.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: And the central figure is particularly significant.
blocks.directed: And the central figure is particularly significant.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Kālarātrī is a manifestation of the power associated with death and dissolution.
blocks.directed: Kālarātrī is a manifestation of the power associated with death and dissolution.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: But in this setting, that destructive potency becomes an instrument of liberation.
blocks.directed: But in this setting, that destructive potency becomes an instrument of liberation.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The power that ordinarily terrifies the limited individual is reinterpreted as capable of freeing them.
blocks.directed: The power that ordinarily terrifies the limited individual is reinterpreted as capable of freeing them.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Death is not simply an enemy.
blocks.directed: Death is not simply an enemy.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Within the ritual theology, the transformative power associated with death can become the very instrument of release.
blocks.directed: Within the ritual theology, the transformative power associated with death can become the very instrument of release.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: That's a beautiful and unsettling reversal.
blocks.directed: That's a beautiful and unsettling reversal.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: ### 7.4 The ritual culminates in identity with Paramaśiva
blocks.directed: ### 7.4 The ritual culminates in identity with Paramaśiva

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: *Tantrasāra* 15.3 states that the individual, having departed through the initiation, becomes non-different from Paramaśiva.
blocks.directed: *Tantrasāra* 15.3 states that the individual, having departed through the initiation, becomes non-different from Paramaśiva.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The crucial Sanskrit phrase is:
blocks.directed: [short pause] The crucial Sanskrit phrase is:

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: *jīvo niṣkrāntaḥ paramaśivābhinno bhavati.*
blocks.directed: *jīvo niṣkrāntaḥ paramaśivābhinno bhavati.*

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: "The departed individual becomes non-different from Paramaśiva."
blocks.directed: [short pause] "The departed individual becomes non-different from Paramaśiva."

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: There.
blocks.directed: There.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: That is the stated destination.
blocks.directed: That is the stated destination.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Not simply a celestial region.
blocks.directed: Not simply a celestial region.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Not merely the continuation of personal memories.
blocks.directed: Not merely the continuation of personal memories.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Not a more pleasant postmortem life.
blocks.directed: Not a more pleasant postmortem life.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The intended result is non-difference from the absolute.
blocks.directed: The intended result is non-difference from the absolute.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: But notice the exact philosophical problem.
blocks.directed: But notice the exact philosophical problem.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: If the individual is ultimately already a manifestation of Śiva, how can they *become* non-different?
blocks.directed: If the individual is ultimately already a manifestation of Śiva, how can they *become* non-different?

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The answer requires distinguishing ontological identity from realized or ritually effected freedom.
blocks.directed: The answer requires distinguishing ontological identity from realized or ritually effected freedom.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The absolute nature is not newly manufactured.
blocks.directed: The absolute nature is not newly manufactured.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: What changes is the condition of the finite individual, specifically their bondage and relation to the manifestation of that absolute.
blocks.directed: What changes is the condition of the finite individual, specifically their bondage and relation to the manifestation of that absolute.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Thus the phrase should not be interpreted as the production of an entirely new divine substance.
blocks.directed: Thus the phrase should not be interpreted as the production of an entirely new divine substance.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The ritual is understood to accomplish the dissolution of limitation.
blocks.directed: The ritual is understood to accomplish the dissolution of limitation.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: That is the deeper logic of Śaiva liberation.
blocks.directed: That is the deeper logic of Śaiva liberation.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: ### 7.5 A further complication: liberation versus enjoyment
blocks.directed: ### 7.5 A further complication: liberation versus enjoyment

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: *Tantrasāra* 15.4-5 distinguishes the individual seeking liberation from one seeking *bhoga*, enjoyment or experience.
blocks.directed: *Tantrasāra* 15.4-5 distinguishes the individual seeking liberation from one seeking *bhoga*, enjoyment or experience.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: This matters enormously.
blocks.directed: This matters enormously.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The ritual technologies can be directed toward different outcomes.
blocks.directed: The ritual technologies can be directed toward different outcomes.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: One person seeks the complete end of bondage.
blocks.directed: One person seeks the complete end of bondage.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Another seeks a favorable condition of existence or spiritual enjoyment.
blocks.directed: Another seeks a favorable condition of existence or spiritual enjoyment.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The tradition does not simply flatten them into one category.
blocks.directed: The tradition does not simply flatten them into one category.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: This is also an important comparison with Tibetan phowa.
blocks.directed: This is also an important comparison with Tibetan phowa.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: A practitioner may aspire to a buddhafield, while another form of the practice emphasizes immediate recognition of the nature of mind.
blocks.directed: A practitioner may aspire to a buddhafield, while another form of the practice emphasizes immediate recognition of the nature of mind.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: Similarly, the Śaiva ritual distinguishes the destination or condition sought by the individual.
blocks.directed: Similarly, the Śaiva ritual distinguishes the destination or condition sought by the individual.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: But the metaphysical content differs.
blocks.directed: But the metaphysical content differs.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: In Trika, identity with Paramaśiva is not the same as reaching a particularly desirable world within manifestation.
blocks.directed: In Trika, identity with Paramaśiva is not the same as reaching a particularly desirable world within manifestation.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: A realm, however exalted, is still describable in terms of an experienced condition.
blocks.directed: A realm, however exalted, is still describable in terms of an experienced condition.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: The supreme reality is not just the highest item on a cosmic property website.
blocks.directed: The supreme reality is not just the highest item on a cosmic property website.

blocks.section: Chapter Seven. Tantrāloka XIX: Abhinavagupta's extraordinary
blocks.text: And that brings us to one of the most beautiful features of the text.
blocks.directed: And that brings us to one of the most beautiful features of the text.

blocks.text: The mantra is characterized as being of the nature of reflective awareness.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: ### 8.1 Why does a mantra have any metaphysical power?
blocks.directed: ### 8.1 Why does a mantra have any metaphysical power?

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: Within Trika, language is not simply a human convention laid upon an independently existing universe.
blocks.directed: Within Trika, language is not simply a human convention laid upon an independently existing universe.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: At its deepest level, the capacity for expression belongs to Śakti.
blocks.directed: At its deepest level, the capacity for expression belongs to Śakti.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: Manifestation itself can be understood through the relation between consciousness, self-articulation and the differentiation of sound and meaning.
blocks.directed: Manifestation itself can be understood through the relation between consciousness, self-articulation and the differentiation of sound and meaning.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: This does not mean that every ordinary utterance possesses the same transformative power.
blocks.directed: This does not mean that every ordinary utterance possesses the same transformative power.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: The distinction between ordinary linguistic use and spiritually effective mantra is part of the tantric system.
blocks.directed: The distinction between ordinary linguistic use and spiritually effective mantra is part of the tantric system.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: But the fundamental claim is that **language is not ontologically foreign to consciousness**.
blocks.directed: But the fundamental claim is that **language is not ontologically foreign to consciousness**.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: A mantra, understood through the proper knowledge and initiation, can function as a vehicle of recognition.
blocks.directed: A mantra, understood through the proper knowledge and initiation, can function as a vehicle of recognition.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: It is not merely transmitting information to a listener.
blocks.directed: It is not merely transmitting information to a listener.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: It is understood as activating a capacity already intrinsic to consciousness.
blocks.directed: It is understood as activating a capacity already intrinsic to consciousness.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: Now consider the deathbed situation.
blocks.directed: Now consider the deathbed situation.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: The individual may be losing the faculties through which ordinary instruction operates.
blocks.directed: The individual may be losing the faculties through which ordinary instruction operates.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: But the tradition does not understand the deepest capacity for awareness as reducible to those faculties.
blocks.directed: But the tradition does not understand the deepest capacity for awareness as reducible to those faculties.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: So a properly empowered utterance is understood as capable of awakening a recognition that is more fundamental than normal sensory comprehension.
blocks.directed: So a properly empowered utterance is understood as capable of awakening a recognition that is more fundamental than normal sensory comprehension.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: That is the theological theory.
blocks.directed: That is the theological theory.

blocks.text: It is not evidence that an unresponsive patient can necessarily hear or understand everything said around them.
blocks.directed: It is not evidence that an unresponsive patient can necessarily hear or understand everything said around them.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: But it reveals something remarkable about the tradition's conception of mantra.
blocks.directed: But it reveals something remarkable about the tradition's conception of mantra.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: The ultimate purpose of the sacred utterance is not simply auditory stimulation.
blocks.directed: The ultimate purpose of the sacred utterance is not simply auditory stimulation.

blocks.section: Chapter Eight. The Brahmavidyā whispered into the dying pers
blocks.text: It is the awakening of self-recognition.
blocks.directed: It is the awakening of self-recognition.

blocks.text: Part III can go even deeper into *Pratyabhijñā* and the actual metaphysics of dying: Utpaladeva's theory of the continuing subject, Kṣemarāja's *Spanda* interpretation, the subtle body's persistence, Abhinavagupta's distinction between individual and divine agency, and the question of whether a liberated master could meaningfully perceive or act after physical death. We can then bring in Mahāmudrā and Dzogchen's very different accounts of primordial awareness.
